items.title: An Engineering Manifesto for AI-Assisted SAP Development — Let's Build It Together
items.author: deiamolina
items.text:
AI helps us learn and write code. We have been shipping code faster than ever. Someone with no IT background can create software now. But software is not just code. It is structure, security, governance and much more. We deal with sensitive data. An error, a security breach can break a company. 
 How can we make AI help us while keeping your company's standards and quality criteria? How can we make sure that all developers, including 3rd-party companies, are using the same naming conventions, the same logic — thinking about governance, quality, and owning their work? 
 I created an Engineering Manifesto for AI-assisted SAP development and a naming convention file too. Both are markdowns files. I'm only sharing 19 of the principles here since many things are company-specific. I'm certain there's much more to add — and that's exactly why I'm here. 
 I'm sharing this for multiple reasons: to help you if you don't have AI rules yet, to learn from you since some of these technologies are new and still evolving for all of us, and we'd love a human-in-the-loop from the community 
 So get ready — read it, challenge it, and let's build something the whole SAP community can use.

items.title: Target Server Selection in SAP Readiness Check Data Collection
items.author: astridtschense
items.text:
We are excited to announce a significant improvement to the data collection process for SAP Readiness Check analyses. The SAP Readiness Check data collection report now includes a Target Server/Server Group selection field on the analysis selection screen. Users can choose a specific application server or server group from the available batch infrastructure, and all applicable background jobs triggered by the analysis run will be submitted to that target. Also, when a target is selected, the Financial Data Quality (FDQ) sub-check automatically recalculates its recommended parallel job count based on the work processes available on that server or group, helping users configure an optimal setup before scheduling. 
 Please note that certain data collectors require prerequisite SAP Note versions or software component patch levels in order for the target server functionality to work: 
 Financial Data Quality (FDQ): SAP Note 2972792 , version 83 or higher 
 HANA Sizing: SAP Note 3675084 
 Data Volume Management (DVM): ST-PI 740 SP 33 or higher, and St-A/PI 01X_731 SP 1 or higher These requirements are also captured within the change log of SAP Note 2758146 . This enhancement gives Basis teams and project administrators greater control over where the Readiness Check analysis jobs execute, making it easy to dedicate a specific server or batch group to the collection workload and avoid resource contention during productive hours. 
 As always, we look forward to receiving your feedback. 
 Your SAP Readiness Check Team

items.title: SAP PaPM Cloud Standard Model – Joule AI Agent: Environment and Process Management Capabilities
items.author: Milan_Mladenovic
items.text:
Hello, SAP Community members! 
 We are excited to announce that Joule, the AI assistant embedded in SAP Profitability and Performance Management Cloud Standard Model (SAP PaPM Cloud SM), is now available in two additional applications: Environment and Process Management . 
 In previous releases, Joule was available in Report Management , where it helped you analyze report data and generate insights. With this expansion, Joule is now your AI assistant in two additional applications, making it faster and more intuitive to navigate and accomplish tasks in Environment and Process Management. 
 This blog post walks you through all Joule capabilities available on these two applications. If you are looking for the technical integration and setup steps (SAP AI Core, SAP Launchpad, BTP Destination), please refer to our previous blog post: 
 SAP PaPM Cloud SM: Joule Setup Guide – BTP Configuration and Application 
 General Joule Features 
 Joule in Environment and Process Management is the same Joule available in Report Management — the conversation panel , its features, and the underlying AI are shared across all three applications . The following general features are available wherever Joule is enabled: 
 Conversation History Sidebar – Browse, rename, delete, and resume past conversations; start a new one at any time. 
 File Upload – Upload external files (up to 5 files, 5 MB each) and ask Joule to analyze them alongside your application data. 
 Web Search – When activated by your administrator, Joule can search the internet and return cited results. 
 Conversation Controls – Stop an ongoing response, switch to fullscreen mode, and use follow-up question suggestions. 
 Your Joule Rules – Set personal instructions in the Joule settings — such as preferred language, response style, or level of detail — and Joule applies them automatically to every new conversation. 
 Guided Help - When needed, Joule consults the official SAP PaPM Cloud Standard Model documentation on the SAP Help Portal to answer your questions — giving you accurate, up-to-date guidance directly in the conversation, without leaving the application. 
 For detailed descriptions of all these features, see: SAP PaPM Cloud Standard Model: Joule AI – Features and Capabilities in Report Management . 
 Opening Joule and Choosing a Mode 
 To open Joule in any Joule-enabled application, choose the Joule icon in the header toolbar. The Joule conversation panel opens on the right side of the screen. 
 Before sending your first message, choose how Joule operates using the Ask / Act toggle in the message input area: 
 Ask – Read-only mode. Joule answers your questions and retrieves information, but does not make any changes to your data. 
 Act – Action mode. Joule can perform operations on your behalf, such as creating, editing, or deleting records. 
 You can switch between Ask and Act at any point in the conversation. 
 Notes: 
 All actions performed by Joule in Act mode are bound by your existing user authorizations. Joule does not elevate your permissions — if you do not have access to a resource, Joule cannot act on it either. 
 Actions performed in Act mode are done in the background. The screen does not refresh automatically, so refresh the Environment or Process Management screen to see the changes reflected in the list 
 Joule Across Applications 
 Joule is a single, unified AI assistant shared across all Joule-enabled applications in SAP Profitability and Performance Management Cloud Standard Model. Two capabilities highlight this: 
 Shared conversation history – Every conversation you start in Joule is accessible from any Joule-enabled application. A conversation you began in Report Management can be continued from Environment or Process Management without losing context — and vice versa. 
 Cross-application actions – You can ask Joule to perform actions on a different screen than the one you are currently on. For example, while working in Environment, you can ask Joule to create a process instance in Process Management — without navigating away from the current screen. 
 Joule in the Environment Application 
 The Environment screen displays the full list of available environments in SAP Profitability and Performance Management Cloud Standard Model, organized in a tree structure of nodes and environments. With Joule, you can explore, create, and manage both nodes and environments through natural language conversation. 
 Asking Questions (Ask Mode) 
 In Ask mode, Joule helps you explore and understand your environments and nodes. Ask it to list, filter, or describe environments based on any criteria. 
 Example questions: 
 "List all private environments." 
 "Show me all environments in the RMS node." 
 "List environments containing reports." 
 "What actions can I perform in the Environment application?" 
 The last example is particularly useful: ask Joule what it can do in the current application, and it will describe all available capabilities in full. 

 Taking Actions (Act Mode) 
 In Act mode, Joule can perform the following operations in the Environment application: 
 Create environment/node – Specify the name, description, and other properties. You can create up to 50 environments in a single request; for larger quantities, Joule executes in multiple batches, each requiring your approval. 
 Edit environment/node – Update the description of an environment or node. 
 Move environment/node – Relocate an environment or node to a different parent node in the tree. 
 Copy environment – Create a copy of an existing environment with a new ID and version. 
 Mark as private or public – Change the access level between Public (visible to all users) and Private (restricted to authorized teams only). 
 Assign a team – Set or update which teams are authorized to access a private environment. 
 Delete environment/node – Remove an environment or an empty node. Because this is a destructive action, Joule lists exactly what will be deleted and asks for your explicit confirmation before proceeding. 
 Note : Joule inherits your role assignments. For example, if you hold the ENVIRONMENTS_READ role only, Joule can view environments but cannot create, edit, or delete them. 

 Joule in the Process Management Application 
 The Process Management screen displays all process instances in a table, along with a Gantt diagram for visualizing timelines. With Joule, you can explore your process data and manage instances and activities through natural language conversation. 
 Asking Questions (Ask Mode) 
 In Ask mode, Joule helps you navigate and understand your process data. You can ask about templates, instances, activities, parameters, states, assigned teams, or any other process-related information. 
 Example questions: 
 "List all deployed process instances in the BAC environment, version 0001." 
 "What is the current state of the Monthly_Close_May process?" 
 "Show me all activities assigned to Team_A." 
 "What are the parameters configured for process instance PROC06?" 

 Taking Actions (Act Mode) 
 In Act mode, Joule can perform the following operations on your process instances and activities: 
 Create process instance from a template – Specify the template, process ID, description, type (Run or Simulation), and start date. You can create up to 50 instances at once; for larger quantities, Joule executes in multiple batches, each requiring your approval. 
 Create process instance from an existing instance – Clone an existing process instance as the starting point for the new one, inheriting its configuration. 
 Create process instance with adjusted selections and parameters – Fine-tune selections and parameter values when creating a new instance, without having to edit each field afterward through the UI. 
 Edit an activity – Update the state, performer team, reviewer team, start date, or end date of an activity. 
 Edit a process instance – Update the description, state, type (Run or Simulation), or start date of a process instance. 
 Note: Joule inherits your role assignments. For example, if you hold the PROCESSES_OWN role only, Joule can manage only your own process instances. 

 Closing Thoughts 
 Joule in SAP Profitability and Performance Management Cloud Standard Model is now available across Report Management , Environment and Process Management applications . All capabilities are authorization-aware and operate within your existing user permissions. 
 Whether you are setting up new environments for a planning cycle, managing process instance activities, or analyzing report data, Joule is there to help you work faster and more confidently — all through natural language. 
 Useful Links 
 Blog Posts: 
 SAP PaPM Cloud SM: Joule Setup Guide – BTP Configuration and Application Settings 
 SAP PaPM Cloud Standard Model: Joule AI – Features and Capabilities in Report Management 
 SAP PaPM Cloud Standard Model: Introducing the AI Conversation Monitor 
 Help Portal: 
 Joule in Standard Model 
 Joule in Environment 
 Joule in Process Management 
 Joule in Report Management 
 Stay tuned — we will continue expanding Joule capabilities across SAP Profitability and Performance Management Cloud Standard Model. Thank you for reading!

items.title: CDS Performance Analysis Understanding Dependencies and Complexity Metrics
items.author: Prabhat_A
items.text:
CDS Performance Analysis – Understanding Dependencies and Complexity 
 ABAP CDS enables powerful Code Pushdown , but using CDS does not automatically guarantee optimal performance. In real-world scenarios, complex CDS stacks can contain multiple layers, joins, associations, calculations, and database sources, making performance issues difficult to identify. 
 In this article, we take a practical Sales Order Analytics example and explore how to analyze a CDS using the Dependency Analyzer in ADT . We will look at the SQL Dependency Tree, SQL Dependency Graph, and Complexity Metrics to understand what happens behind the scenes and identify potential areas for optimization. 
 This is the first part of a practical CDS Performance Tuning series, where we build the foundation for analyzing the generated SQL and execution plan in the upcoming articles.

items.title: Approve With Context: How AI Process Comparison Closes the Process Review Gap
items.author: amitsharma19
items.text:
Approve With Context: How AI Process Comparison Closes the Process Review Gap 
 There is a moment every process owner knows. 
 You receive a change request. The updated diagram is attached. You open it, open the previous version in another tab, and spend the next hour squinting at lanes, switching back and forth, hoping you notice every difference before you sign off. 
 Sometimes you catch everything. Sometimes you don't. Either way, you spent three hours on something that should have taken ten minutes. 
 That gap between what approval requires and what is actually possible in a reasonable time is exactly what the new AI Process Comparison action in SAP Signavio Process Governance is designed to close. 
 The Problem With Reviewing Process Changes 
 Process diagrams are not documents. They are networks. A change in one lane can ripple into responsibilities, system handoffs, compliance controls, and SLA commitments in ways that a quick visual scan will not catch. 
 Ask anyone who has signed off on a process update without fully understanding it. The risk is not that they approved intentionally. The risk is that they approved without knowing what they were approving. 
 And the effort is real. Based on SAP expert estimation, a typical process owner spends 3 hours per change request review . For a team of five owners handling two requests each per month, that adds up fast, and most of that time is spent not on judgment, but on information gathering: what actually changed? 
 Introducing AI Process Comparison 
 We now have AI Process Comparison as a built-in external action in SAP Signavio Process Governance, and we have been adding it to governance workflows wherever change review matters. 
 You configure it like any other step. Point it at two process IDs, or two revisions of the same process, and when that step runs, the AI analyzes both diagrams and returns a structured report covering: 
 What was added to the second process 
 What was removed from the first 
 The business impact of those changes 
 The approver does not need to open the diagram editor. They do not need to compare versions manually. By the time the task reaches their queue, the work of understanding what changed is already done. 
 Seeing It Work 
 We wired up a full end-to-end flow using the Order to Deliver process to show what this looks like in practice. Here is exactly what happened: 
 1. A process modeler submitted an updated version of the Order to Deliver process for approval, triggering a governance workflow in SAP Signavio Process Governance. 

 2. The workflow created a new approval case and routed it to the approver's queue 

 3. The approver opened the task and saw the inputs: the current revision ID and the revision it was being compared against. 

 4. In the background, the AI began analyzing both diagram versions automatically, with no manual trigger and no waiting. 
 5. Within moments, the comparison result appeared in the task. Here is what the AI produced: 
 Added: Tasks related to strategic planning, including "Draft Go-to-market tactics", "Organize SC/PC Planning meetings", and "Review, validate and activate SC annual plan", introducing a complex strategic management workflow. Collaboration between Sales Center and Product Center participants enabling cross-departmental alignment on market tactics. Multiple start events triggered by market changes or strategy updates, allowing for dynamic process initiation. 
 Removed: Tasks "Receive order", "Forward order to sales", "Notify seller", "Pack order", "Transfer package to operations", and "Hand over to delivery personnel", which managed the physical order fulfillment flow. The Customer Service, Operations Team, Sales Department, and Seller lanes, removing the operational fulfillment structure entirely. 
 Impact: The process has shifted from a linear order fulfillment workflow to a complex strategic planning and go-to-market management process, replacing operational tasks with strategic coordination and planning activities. 

 6. The output is clearly marked as AI-generated, prompting the reviewer to verify before approving. That label keeps the human in the loop without slowing the process down the AI does the reading, the approver does the judging. 
 7. The approver read the report, had everything they needed, and selected approve 
 End-to-end. Submission to decision in minutes, not hours. Zero manual comparison steps. 
 What the Numbers Say 
 The impact is not subtle. AI Process Comparison reduces time spent reviewing process diagram change requests by 70% , from 3 hours to 54 minutes per review per process owner FTE. 
 For a consumer products company with €1 billion in revenue and five process owner FTEs, that translates to approximately €7k in annual savings from review time alone, based on SAP benchmark assumptions. 
 The more significant number, though, is not the time saved. It is the risk reduced. Faster reviews done with AI-generated context are more accurate than slower reviews done without it. 
 How to Set It Up 
 We configure AI Process Comparison under Organization Settings > Actions > AI Process Comparison . 
 Prerequisites: 
 AI terms and conditions accepted under Workspace Settings > AI Services 
 Modeling - Joule: Generate Process Description enabled under Workspace Settings > Feature Access 

 Full setup guide for org admins: Enabling Compare Diagrams 
 Configuration: 
 Once enabled, you add it to your governance workflow through the External Actions menu ( full reference ). The action takes two inputs: 
 Input Description 
 First Process ID The baseline, the version you're comparing from 
 Second Process ID The new version, or a specific revision ID 

 It returns two outputs: an operation success confirmation, and the Comparison Result text, which is the structured report of additions, removals, and impact that flows into the approver's task view. 
 No custom middleware. No export step. No manual document to prepare. It runs as part of the governance workflow itself. 
 More Than Approval Workflows 
 Approval is the obvious starting point, but we see process comparison adding value at any governance checkpoint where understanding change matters: 
 Compliance audits: generate a documented diff between as-is and to-be diagrams as evidence 
 Post-change review: compare before and after an SAP implementation or process transformation 
 Onboarding: help new team members understand how a process evolved 
 Change communication: use the AI-generated summary as the basis for stakeholder notifications 
 Process governance has always been about making the right decisions at the right time. AI Process Comparison makes sure those decisions are informed ones. 
 Give it a shot 
 AI Process Comparison is available now in SAP Signavio Process Governance. Enable it in your Organization Settings and add it to any approval workflow where change clarity matters. 
 If you want to explore how this fits into your governance setup, reach out. And if you want to see the full flow first, we have a short end-to-end demo showing submission to approval in under two minutes. 

 Check out our post on BPMN Export a feature we released last month that automatically exports your process diagrams in XML, PNG, SVG, or PDF the moment a governance milestone is reached. We wired it up to a full AI translation pipeline with n8n and SAP AI Core to show what it can drive.

items.title: Update on SAPUI5 / OpenUI5 2.x: Best-Practice Code Is Your Best Strategy
items.author: OliverGraeff
items.text:
In late 2023, we introduced OpenUI5 2.x with a clear goal: renew the UI5 framework by removing deprecated libraries and functionality, making it leaner, faster, and future-proof. Since then, the UI5 team has made significant progress towards this legacy-free vision — from cleaning up the core to providing tooling that helps you modernize your applications. This post is an update on where we stand with SAPUI5 / OpenUI5 2.x and what it means for you. 

 SAPUI5 / OpenUI5 2.x delivery is on hold 
 UI5 2.x is currently on hold from a delivery perspective. The technical work is largely done. We have cleaned up the framework, removed synchronous APIs, eliminated globals, and followed internally the same rules we ask you to follow externally. The migration tooling achieves a very high percentage of automatic conversion rates for application code. From a pure readiness standpoint, we could ship. 
 However, the rapid evolution of AI has fundamentally changed the questions we need to answer. What does the future programming model look like for an AI-native user experience? How should application design evolve? How do we best address the challenges and opportunities that AI brings to UI development? UI5 2.x is legacy-free, and that has clear advantages — but it is not fundamentally different from the current stack. From an AI perspective, it would not solve additional problems compared to what UI5 1.x already provides today. If we want to bring something genuinely new, addressing different problems, we likely need to do more than what version 2.x set out to do. 
 We have therefore decided to put the delivery on hold and use this opportunity to explore how the UI5 framework can be positioned to play a best-in-class role in an AI-driven environment. 
 SAPUI5 remains SAP's strategic UI technology for building applications. We want to make sure it continues to play a key role in the AI age. 

 The foundational work pays off 
 While the delivery of SAPUI5 2.x as a separate version is on hold, the foundational work we have done is far from wasted — it is already paying off today. 
 Legacy-free cleanup across the stack. We have cleaned up the UI5 core, synchronous module loading (to the extent possible in a compatible way) and globals, and deprecating non-compliant APIs. The basic UI5 libraries are legacy-free, the SAP Fiori launchpad provides a new sandbox with async services, and the SAP Fiori elements cleanup is underway. 
 UI5 linter. With a single command, you get an audit of your application that that tells you what needs to be corrected to comply with UI5 best practices. The linter also includes an autofix capability for deterministic fixes. 
 UI5 Modernization AI skills. What the linter cannot fix automatically, AI takes further. The UI5 Modernization Plugin for coding agents (e.g. for Claude Code or GitHub Copilot) run the linter, scan for solutions, and execute code changes to clean up your codebase. Together with the UI5 Linter autofix option, this achieves a very high percentage of automated migrations to legacy-free best practices. While manual testing is still required, we continue to close the remaining gaps. 
 These tools and the cleaned-up codebase benefit you regardless of how the UI5 versioning evolves. Following UI5 best practices — TypeScript first, asynchronous loading, no globals — makes your applications better, future-proof and ready for what comes next. 

 What you should do 

 The message is clear: keep modernizing your applications. The foundational work towards legacy-free is valuable today and will carry forward. 
 Follow UI5 best practices : TypeScript first, asynchronous loading, no globals, no deprecated APIs.

items.title: SAP Joule Work mobile app version 3.2 brings exciting new features
items.author: ThiloBerndt
items.text:
Let's have a look at the new features that got released for both experiences, the Joule Work experience, as well as the SAP Build Work Zone experience – formally called SAP Mobile Start. 
 Let´s start with the features that are valid for both experiences. 

 With the latest release, Joule conversations are now shared between mobile and web , meaning you can start a conversation on mobile and then continue it on your laptop or desktop computer. Certainly, also expired conversations will be available on mobile and web. 
 The new Profile and Settings entry “Conversations” allows you to see your user profile data and to enable/ disable the Joule memory feature right in the mobile app. When turned on, Joule remembers your preferences, workflows, and chat goals to keep responses relevant and fast. Memories are usually kept for 12 months, but you can revoke consent anytime by deactivating its toggle, then the memories are deleted immediately. You can always see the stored data under “Saved Memories”. 

 Screenshot: New setting entry for conversations: Memory 
 You can now engage in natural voice conversations with Joule Work in the mobile app. With the latest release, you can speak directly to Joule and receive spoken responses, eliminating the need to look at your device screen. This hands-free experience is particularly useful when you are on the go or need to work without interacting with your device. The new Apple CarPlay integration also enables you to communicate with Joule while driving—for example, to prepare for your next customer meeting. 

 Screenshot: Joule Work in Apple Carplay 
 Since the last release, we allow you to customize the Support Section on the "Profile and Settings" screen. This allows you to add additional information for your users, in case they have any support needs. Now, administrators can additionally add free text to this section. Once configured, the info is displayed on the Profile and Settings screen as well as during the onboarding process. The feature can be added and configured via SAP Mobile Services or via Mobile Device Management (MDM) . Please also check our SAP Help documentation for details. 
 Finally, administrators can select a dedicated browser via MDM for the onboarding process. This feature can be used to define the browser the Joule Work mobile app uses for the initial onboarding authentication and possible re-authentication and allows you to enforce a specific browser policy across your managed device fleet. The setting does not affect the general in-app browsing behavior. 
 We also have added Thai to the list of supported languages for SAP Joule mobile app. 
 Next, let´s have a look at the new feature for only Joule Work experience. 

 You can now view insights on your spaces and cards. Just tap on the overflow menu (three dots) of a space and select “Open Insights”. Then the insights overlay appears and provides info such as which steps got executed and which sources got leveraged to create the space. 

 Screenshot: Insights on Spaces 
 Finally, what is new for SAP Build Work Zone experience? 

 With the last release we had introduced workspaces for SAP Build Work Zone, advanced edition. Since then, you can easily access your workspaces when being away from your desk with the Joule Work mobile app. Now, you can also add your favorite workspaces to the Start screen, with your changes synced automatically across mobile and web. To add a workspace to the Start screen, just do a long tap on a workspace tile and add it – the same way you know from adding app favorites. 
 I hope you will enjoy these features in the Joule Work mobile app. 
 Visit SAP Mobile Experience Community Page and click “follow” to get the latest development and innovation of our solutions. We look forward to hearing about your experience with setting up the solution in your landscape; please do share your thoughts and comments below. Enter here for additional questions regarding SAP Mobile Experience Applications. 
 Want to be notified? Check your profile settings to ensure you have your settings activated.

items.title: Unboxing Joule Studio: Exploring the jl CLI : Your First Steps
items.author: Yogananda
items.text:
SAP's Joule Studio ships with two development paths: a visual, browser-based low-code builder and a terminal-driven pro-code flow. The jl CLI is the engine behind the latter — giving developers full control over the entire capability lifecycle from the command line. 
 What Is the Joule Studio CLI? 
 The Joule Studio CLI ( jl ) is a globally installed npm package that lets you scaffold, validate, compile, deploy, and manage custom Joule capabilities without ever opening a browser. It's the tool of choice for developers who prefer working directly with YAML, want to integrate Joule into CI/CD pipelines, or need a headless, automation-friendly workflow. SAP Architecture Center 
 The jl CLI is also referred to as the joule command in some SAP documentation and samples — both point to the same package. 
 Prerequisites 
 Before you install the CLI, you'll need: 
 Node.js v22.10.0 – v26.x (verify with node --version ; use nvm use 20 if you manage versions via nvm) 
 npm (bundled with Node.js) 
 Access to a Joule Studio environment on SAP BTP 
 Installation 
 Install the CLI globally from npm: 
 npm install -g @sap/joule-work-dev-cli-early-adopters@latest 
 Verify the installation: 
 jl version
# or
jl -V 
 The Help Output — At a Glance 

 Running jl help gives you the full command surface in one shot: 
 Usage: jl [options] [command]

Solution Management CLI

Options:
 -h, --help display help for command

Commands:
 solution|s Manage solutions
 asset|a Manage assets
 mcp Manage MCP servers
 a2a Agent-to-agent communication
 init [options] [agent] [path] Initialise a directory for an AI coding agent
 skills Manage agent skills
 login [url] Log in to a backend
 logout [url] Log out from the current backend
 info [options] Show CLI version and active backend connection
 version|v Show the jl client version number
 help [command] display help for command

 ASSET TYPES

 agent Agent asset — AI agent with container and health probe configuration
 agent-extension Agent extension asset — extends a base agent with additional capabilities
 base-ui Base UI asset — AppRouter-based frontend web application (Next.js, React, etc.)
 cap-app CAP application asset — Node.js CAP service with container and health probe configuration
 data-product Data product asset — data consumption and production with governance configuration
 domain-model-extension Domain model extension asset — adds custom fields to existing CAP entities
 mcp-server MCP server asset — API-to-MCP tool mapping (type: mcp-translation, asset.yaml + translation.json + api-spec.json)
 n8n-workflow n8n workflow asset — n8n automation workflow integration
 vercel-app Vercel app asset — Vercel-deployed frontend application

 Names must be DNS-compatible: lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens only (1–63 chars).

 SHORTCUTS

 s → solution
 a → asset
 v → version

 EXAMPLES

 jl login 'https://my-backend.cfapps.eu12.hana.ondemand.com?issuerUrl=https://myias.accounts.cloud.sap&clientId=<id>&appTid=<tid>'
 jl solution create --name my-solution
 jl solution build
 jl solution deploy
 jl solution deploy ./build/my-solution-1.0.0.zip
 jl solution list
 jl solution deploy status
 jl solution deploy logs --tail 100
 jl mcp tools n8n-mcp
 jl mcp call n8n-mcp validate-n8n-workflow workflow="..."
 jl mcp call n8n-mcp validate-n8n-workflow --params args.json
 jl asset create agent --name my-agent
 jl asset create cap-app --name my-service
 jl asset create mcp-server --name my-mcp
 jl asset delete my-agent
 jl solution validate
 jl info 
 Command Groups — What Each One Does 
 jl login / logout 
 Authentication is the first step in every session. You pass your landscape URL (including IAS issuer, client ID, and app tenant ID) directly in the command: 
 jl login 'https://my-backend.cfapps.eu12.hana.ondemand.com?issuerUrl=https://myias.accounts.cloud.sap&clientId=<id>&appTid=<tid>' 

 This initiates an OAuth 2.0 auth-code flow and stores credentials locally for subsequent commands. Use jl logout to clear them. 
 jl solution (shortcut: jl s ) 
 The solution command group is the heart of the workflow — it handles the full lifecycle of a Joule solution: 
 jl solution create --name my-solution # Scaffold a new solution
jl solution validate # Check solution artifacts for errors
jl solution build # Compile into a deployable .zip
jl solution deploy # Deploy to your connected backend
jl solution deploy ./build/my-solution-1.0.0.zip # Deploy a specific build artifact
jl solution list # List deployed solutions
jl solution deploy status # Check deployment status
jl solution deploy logs --tail 100 # Stream the last 100 deployment log lines 
 jl asset (shortcut: jl a ) 
 Assets are the building blocks that compose a solution. The CLI supports nine distinct asset types: Asset Type Description 
 agent AI agent with container and health probe configuration 
 agent-extension Extends a base agent with additional capabilities 
 base-ui AppRouter-based frontend (Next.js, React, etc.) 
 cap-app Node.js CAP service with container and health probe config 
 data-product Data consumption and production with governance config 
 domain-model-extension Adds custom fields to existing CAP entities 
 mcp-server API-to-MCP tool mapping (asset.yaml + translation.json + api-spec.json) 
 n8n-workflow n8n automation workflow integration 
 vercel-app Vercel-deployed frontend application 
 Asset names must be DNS-compatible: lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens only (1–63 characters). 
 jl asset create agent --name my-agent
jl asset create cap-app --name my-service
jl asset create mcp-server --name my-mcp
jl asset delete my-agent 
 jl mcp 
 The mcp command lets you inspect and interact with MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers wired into your solution — useful for testing tool bindings before deploying: 
 jl mcp tools n8n-mcp # List available tools on the MCP server
jl mcp call n8n-mcp validate-n8n-workflow workflow="..." # Call a tool directly
jl mcp call n8n-mcp validate-n8n-workflow --params args.json # Call with params from a file 
 jl a2a 
 The a2a command manages Agent-to-Agent (A2A) communication — the protocol layer used when agents need to delegate work to, or orchestrate, other agents across a Joule landscape. 
 jl init 
 Initialises a directory for a specific AI coding agent (e.g., Claude Code, OpenCode). This sets up the local environment so the agent understands the project structure and can invoke jl commands on your behalf via MCP. 
 jl init [agent] [path] 
 jl skills 
 Manages agent skills — the modular, reusable capability units that agents expose to end users through Joule. 
 jl info 
 A quick diagnostic command that shows the currently active CLI version and the backend connection it's authenticated against: 

 jl info 
 The Pro-Code Development Lifecycle 
 Putting it all together, a typical end-to-end flow looks like this: 
 # 1. Authenticate
jl login '<your-landscape-url>'

# 2. Scaffold a new solution
jl solution create --name my-solution

# 3. Add the assets you need
jl asset create agent --name my-agent
jl asset create cap-app --name my-service

# 4. Author and iterate in your IDE

# 5. Validate before building
jl solution validate

# 6. Build the deployable artifact
jl solution build

# 7. Deploy
jl solution deploy

# 8. Monitor the rollout
jl solution deploy status
jl solution deploy logs --tail 100 
 CI/CD Integration 
 The CLI is designed to be fully scriptable, making it a natural fit for automated pipelines. SAP explicitly positions it for headless environments and DevOps workflows — you can drive the full lint → compile → deploy cycle from a GitHub Actions job, a GitLab CI stage, or any other CI runner. Capability artifacts follow a Git-based workflow: everything lives in source control, and your pipeline calls the CLI commands as standard build steps. SAP News 
 Because every command is non-interactive and scriptable, the CLI drops cleanly into any pipeline runner. A minimal GitHub Actions step might look like: 
 - name: Deploy Joule Solution
 run: |
 jl login '${{ secrets.JOULE_BACKEND_URL }}'
 jl solution validate
 jl solution build
 jl solution deploy 
 Working with AI Coding Agents via MCP 
 In the pro-code flow, the CLI pairs with an AI coding agent (such as Claude Code or OpenCode) connected to your project via the Model Context Protocol (MCP) . The coding agent can read your YAML definitions, suggest changes, and invoke jl commands — while you stay in control of what gets deployed. MCP handles the agent-to-tool connection; A2A (Agent-to-Agent) handles orchestration when multiple agents need to collaborate across a workflow. SAP Architecture Center 
 CLI vs. Low-Code: When to Use Which 
 Low-Code (Browser) Pro-Code ( jl CLI) 
 Setup required None Node.js + npm 
 Authoring Visual drag-and-drop YAML in any IDE 
 Git integration Limited Full 
 CI/CD support No Yes 
 Best for Business configurators, rapid prototyping Developers, DevOps, automation 
 Both paths produce the same deployable artifact and register it with the same Joule runtime — so you can start low-code and migrate to CLI-driven workflows as your project matures. SAP Joule Studio 
 Companion: Visual Studio Code Editor (Claude Code/Opencode Extension) 
 If you prefer working inside an IDE rather than a bare terminal, the jl CLI pairs naturally with Visual Studio Code running Claude Code or OpenCode as your AI coding agent. After running jl init claude (or jl init opencode ), the agent is wired directly into your project via .mcp.json — giving it access to Joule Studio's MCP server and the IBD skills fetched from your backend. 
 In practice this means you can: 
 Let the coding agent scaffold assets, author YAML, and suggest edits inline in your editor 
 Run jl solution validate , jl solution build , and jl solution deploy from the integrated terminal as usual 
 Use the agent's awareness of Joule's asset types and schemas (via the fetched IBD skills) to catch mistakes before they reach the build step 
 The CLI and the coding agent use the same project structure and config — there's no separate format to learn. The agent assists with authoring; the CLI owns build and deploy. SAP Architecture Center 
 Initialize Your Project 
 Create a new folder for your project, enter it, and run jl init with your preferred AI coding agent: 
 mkdir my-project && cd my-project 
 Claude Code 
 jl init claude 
 OpenCode 
 jl init opencode 
 This single command does three things for you: 
 Writes .mcp.json — wires the Joule Studio MCP server into your coding agent 
 Writes .claude/settings.local.json (or equivalent) — configures agent-level settings for the project 
 Fetches the IBD (Intent-Based Development) skills from the backend into .claude/skills/ — giving your coding agent domain knowledge about Joule's asset types, YAML schemas, and development patterns 
 VSCode users — two things to keep in mind: 
 Open the project folder directly in VSCode so that .mcp.json sits at the workspace root. Opening it as a subfolder inside a larger multi-root workspace will prevent Claude Code from locating the MCP config. 
 After running jl init claude or making any changes to .mcp.json, run Developer: Reload Window ( Ctrl+Shift+P / Cmd+Shift+P → type "Reload Window") so Claude Code picks up the updated configuration. 
 Once initialised, your project folder will look something like this: 
 my-project/
├── .mcp.json ← MCP server config for the coding agent
└── .claude/
 ├── settings.local.json ← Agent settings (project-scoped)
 └── skills/ ← IBD skills fetched from the backend
 └── ... 
 From here you're ready to start creating assets and building your solution with jl asset create and jl solution build . 
 Summary 
 The jl CLI brings the full Joule capability lifecycle to the terminal. Whether you're authoring YAML by hand, integrating with an AI coding agent over MCP, or wiring capability deployments into a CI/CD pipeline, the CLI gives you the scriptability and precision that production-grade development demands. items.text:
On 26 September 2026 , I had the privilege of attending SAP Inside Track Bengaluru – Business AI Edition at SAP Labs India Innovation Park . Walking into the campus, I already knew it would be a day filled with technology, innovation, and learning—but what I experienced exceeded every expectation. 

 SAP Inside Track is much more than a conference. It is a community-driven platform where developers, architects, consultants, students, customers, partners, and technology enthusiasts come together to Learn. Share. Grow. This year's edition focused entirely on SAP Business AI , highlighting how AI is transforming enterprise applications, automation, and business processes. 

 An Inspiring Beginning 

 The event began with an inspiring keynote by Sindhu Gangadharan , Managing Director of SAP Labs India and Head of Customer Innovation Services at SAP. 

 Listening to her speak about innovation, leadership, the future of enterprise AI, and the role of technology in solving real-world business challenges was incredibly motivating. Her vision of making AI practical, responsible, and accessible across enterprises perfectly set the tone for the rest of the day. 

 Following the keynote, I attended an engaging Coffee Discussion and Q&A session featuring: 

 Amol Palshikar – Google Cloud 

 Anshika Kabra – TechCarvings Consultancy Pvt. Ltd. 

 The discussion went beyond technical concepts. It focused on industry adoption, career growth, cloud technologies, SAP's AI ecosystem, and how organizations are preparing for the future of intelligent enterprises. Having the opportunity to ask questions directly to experienced professionals was one of the highlights of the event. 

 Exploring the Demo Pods 

 One of the most exciting parts of the event was visiting the Demo Pods . 

 I explored demonstrations from: 

 Google Cloud 

 Zaran Technologies 

 Rojo Integrations 

 SAP Concur 

 Each booth showcased real-world business solutions powered by SAP technologies. 

 Instead of simply presenting products, the teams demonstrated practical use cases showing how SAP integrates with different platforms to automate business workflows, improve productivity, simplify enterprise operations, and reduce manual effort. 

 It was fascinating to see how organizations leverage SAP technologies to solve complex business challenges with elegant and scalable solutions. 

 Hands-on Learning 

 Theory becomes meaningful when you can experience it yourself.

items.title: Graph-Based RAG Solution with SAP HANA Cloud Discovery Agents
items.author: Sharathmg
items.text:
Context 
 This article presents practical insights from the SAP Beta Program for SAP HANA Cloud Data and Discovery Agents. The solution combines SAP HANA metadata, knowledge graphs, and vectorized summaries to enable natural-language discovery across semantically related database tables. The exercise involved configuring SAP AI Core connectivity, certificates, triple-store and NLP capabilities, graph-based RAG structures, and role-based access for administrative and agent users. The beta demonstrated promising potential for simplifying data exploration across complex SAP HANA models, while also highlighting important considerations around setup complexity, security privileges, metadata quality, and memory consumption. Further validation is recommended to assess scalability, accuracy, governance, and production readiness. 
 Background of the Beta Program 
 This article is based on my participation in the SAP Beta Program for SAP HANA Cloud Data and Discovery Agents. 
 The purpose of the program was to evaluate new procedures and tools capable of identifying semantic relationships and generating summaries used to respond to natural language queries spanning multiple tables. 
 The project involves building a graph-based RAG dataset from SAP HANA metadata, where database objects and relationships are represented in a knowledge graph, and summaries are vectorized into a RAG table for semantic retrieval and natural language querying. 
 The goal was to prepare the HANA Cloud instance with SAP AI Core, configure certificates, and activate settings to facilitate the discovery agents. 
 Setup 
 High-Level Architecture Press enter or click to view image in full size 

 Flow: 
 User Query → Discovery Agent → SAP AI Core Model → RAG Retrieval & Knowledge Graph → SAP HANA Tables → Response 
 Prerequisites 
 Enable Triple Store and NLP: 
 Note: NLP activation may lead to an increased memory footprint. Press enter or click to view image in full size 

 2. An AI Core instance with the deployment URL: 
 Configure an AI Core Instance: 
 Go to ML Operations > Deployment and create a new deployment configuration. Press enter or click to view image in full size 

 Select the deployment configuration to retrieve the Deployment URL . Press enter or click to view image in full size 

 3. Create Personal Security Environment (PSE) Store and Root Certificates: 
 Follow the SAP AI Core Service Key Setup Guide to create the PSE. 
 Modify the JSON configuration to extend validity to 60 days. 
 { 
 "xsuaa" : { 
 "credential-type" : "x509" , 
 "x509" : { 
 "key-length" : 2048 , 
 "validity" : 60 , 
 "validity-type" : "DAYS" 
 } 
 } 
 } 
 Note: Need a user with DBADMIN privileges (or execution via the DBADMIN user) to run the required SQL statements. Press enter or click to view image in full size 
 Press enter or click to view image in full size 

 Confirm Setup: 
 Execute the confirmation procedure: 
 CALL "Get_Remote_Source_AI_Models"('DISCOVERY_REMOTE_SOURCE', ?); Press enter or click to view image in full size 

 Execution 
 The project includes code setup with synthetic data for tables loaded into the HANA DB via DBX. Python scripts were configured in VS Code to perform the following steps: 
 Metadata File: Create a metadata file listing the database objects. 

 2. Environment Variables: Set the required environment variables: 
 set HANA_HOST=<hana_cloud_instance_id>.hanacloud.ondemand.com 
 set HANA_USER=<agent_admin_user> 
 set HANA_PASSWORD=<agent_admin_user_password> 
 set HANA_AGENT_RAG_TOOL= true 
 set HANA_AGENT_STRUCTURED_PROMPT= true 
 set HANA_AGENT_USE_TABLE_INFORMATION_TOOL= true 
 set HANA_AGENT_USE_RELATED_OBJECTS_TOOL= true 
 set HANA_AGENT_USE_KNOWLEDGE_GRAPH_TOOL= true 
 set HANA_AGENT_USER_SQL_FILTER_VERIFICATION_TOOL= true 
 set TRACE_LEVEL=debug 
 Graph Creation: Create the DISCOVERY_AGENT_SCHEMA and run create_graph.py : 
 python src/graph/create_graph.py --knowledgeGraphName DISCOVERY_AI_KG_EPM --ragSchemaName DISCOVERY_AGENT_SCHEMA --ragTableName DISCOVERY_AI_RAG_EPM_INDEX "<file_path>obj_infos\aiEnabledObjects_EPM_ALL.yaml" 
 Agent User Permissions: Grant execution privileges for the required procedures: 
 SYS.DATA_AGENT_DEV 
 SYS.DISCOVERY_AGENT_DEV 
 Resource Access: Grant access to the remote source, knowledge graph, and RAG table: 
 GRANT EXECUTE ON REMOTE SOURCE < remote_source > TO < user > ; 
 GRANT SPARQL QUERY TO < user > ; 
 CALL SPARQL_EXECUTE( 'GRANT SELECT ON <HANA_OBJECTS> TO <user>' , '' , ?, ?); 
 GRANT SELECT ON "<schema>"."RAG" TO < user > ; 
 Role & User Configuration: 
 AI_ADMIN_ROLE and AI_ADMIN_USER to: 
 Create remote source 
 Create index structures (Object Knowledge Graph, RAG table) 
 Create wrapper procedures 
 Grant privileges to AI_AGENT_USER

 EXECUTE permissions for the remote source 
 READ permissions for index structures 
 EXECUTE permissions for wrapper procedures 
 READ permissions for sample data tables 
 Test Results 
 Invoke the procedure and monitor the query execution results. 
 CALL SYS.DISCOVERY_AGENT_DEV ( 
 'In which position does Mia Nguyen work?' , 
 '{ 
 "remoteSourceName":"DISCOVERY_REMOTE_SOURCE", 
 "knowledgeGraphName":"DISCOVERY_AI_KG_EPM", 
 "ragSchemaName":"DISCOVERY_AGENT_SCHEMA", 
 "ragTableName":"DISCOVERY_AI_RAG_EPM_INDEX" 
 }' , 
 ? 
 ); 

 To answer the question "In which position does Mia Nguyen work?", here is how you can find the answer using the available HANA database objects: 

 1. The table "EPM_DATA"."OrgEmployees" contains employee information, including first and last names, and an "OrgUnitId" column that links each employee to an organizational unit. 
 2. The table "EPM_DATA"."OrgUnits" contains organizational unit information, including "OrgUnitId" and "OrgUnitName". The "OrgUnitName" typically represents the department or position name. 

 Although the sample data does not include "Mia Nguyen", you can use the following approach to find the position for any employee: 

 - Look up the employee in "EPM_DATA"."OrgEmployees" by matching "FirstName" and "LastName" to "Mia" and "Nguyen". 
 - Retrieve the corresponding "OrgUnitId" for that employee. 
 - Join this "OrgUnitId" with "EPM_DATA"."OrgUnits" to get the "OrgUnitName", which represents the position or department. 

 Here are the relevant columns: 

 From "EPM_DATA"."OrgEmployees":

 '{ 
 "remoteSourceName":"DISCOVERY_REMOTE_SOURCE", 
 "knowledgeGraphName":" DISCOVERY_AI_KG_EPM ", 
 "ragSchemaName":"DISCOVERY_AGENT_SCHEMA", 
 "ragTableName":" DISCOVERY_AI_RAG_EPM_INDEX " 
 }' , 
 ?

 Observations & Key Learnings 
 Entry Point: Setting up the SAP AI Core instance and Deployment URLs is the necessary starting point. 
 Memory Footprint: Enabling Triple Store noticeably increases memory consumption. 
 Graph Modeling: Defining proper table linkages inside the Knowledge Graph YAML file is crucial for cross-table relationships. 
 Privilege Management: Explicitly grant table data schema privileges to the execution user. 
 Natural Language Querying: Demonstrates strong potential for running complex queries across semantically related tables using plain language. 
 Thank you to the HANA Cloud team from India and Germany who facilitated this program.

items.title: SAP Named a Leader in the IDC MarketScape: Worldwide Agentic Marketing for B2C Enterprises 2026 Vendor Assessment
items.author: Sara Richter
items.text:
SAP has been named a leader in the IDC MarketScape: Worldwide Agentic Marketing for B2C Enterprises 2026 Vendor Assessment (doc #US54113426, September 2026). 
 Deliver personalized, AI-driven engagement across every channel and touchpoint 

 Learn how 

 We believe this recognition reflects SAP’s commitment to helping enterprises deliver intelligent, personalized customer experiences, enhanced by AI, built on trusted data and connected end-to-end business processes, and grounded in real-life business context. Joule Agents, Joule Assistants, SAP Business Data Cloud , and SAP Engagement Cloud together provide the agentic marketing backbone to advance this vision of the Autonomous Enterprise. 

 AI is evolving from assisting marketers to executing and acting on their behalf, creating a fundamental opportunity for organizations to completely rethink how they engage customers. Agentic marketing enables AI agents and assistants to understand context, take action, and help brands deliver more relevant personalized experiences. 

 Trust is the foundation to this shift. As AI takes on greater responsibility, organizations need solutions built with security, compliance, governance, and trusted business data so customers can confidently rely on AI-driven interactions and decisions. 

 Why agentic marketing matters 

 Consumers are becoming more comfortable using AI, reshaping their expectations of the brands they love and the organizations they interact with. SAP’s 2026 Global Customer Loyalty Index indicates that 33% of consumers now trust AI assistants to complete purchases on their behalf, while 31% say interactions with AI assistants make them more loyal to a brand. The trend is even more pronounced across younger consumers. Across generations, we see AI playing an influential role in purchasing decisions and long-term customer loyalty. For example, a consumer might ask an AI assistant to reorder a household product, book a trip, or recommend a new product based on past preferences. For those interactions to succeed, customers must trust that the AI is acting on accurate information, protecting their data, and making decisions within appropriate guardrails. 

 Organizations from manufacturers to fashion brands are seasoned in using generative AI to create content, build audiences, and improve marketing efficiency. Attention is turning to agentic marketing: moving from AI that recommends to AI that acts. 
 IDC MarketScape vendor analysis model is designed to provide an overview of the competitive fitness of technology and suppliers in a given market. The research methodology utilizes a rigorous scoring methodology based on both qualitative and quantitative criteria that results in a single graphical illustration of each supplier’s position within a given market. The Capabilities score measures supplier product, go-to-market and business execution in the short-term. The Strategy score measures alignment of supplier strategies with customer requirements in a 3-5-year timeframe. Supplier market share is represented by the size of the icons. 

 Marketing context meets business reality 

 Most marketing platforms understand customer interactions well: clicks, opens, purchases, and browsing behavior. Those signals matter, but they only tell part of the story. The most valuable signals often live elsewhere across the enterprise in inventory availability, order status, fulfillment performance, product profitability, return behavior, and subscription and replenishment cycles. 

 Marketing often sees customer behavior, while ERP systems see business reality. The greatest opportunity for AI emerges when those worlds come together. Because SAP sits at the heart of how many of the world’s leading enterprises operate, marketers can access the operational intelligence that lives within the systems running the business, enabling AI to make decisions based not only on what customers are doing, but on what the business can actually deliver. In an age of agentic marketing, that distinction matters. 

 Why SAP was recognized as a Leader 

 SAP was recognized for the following strengths by the IDC MarketScape: 

 With the agentic layer of Joule, marketers get real-time, context-aware personalization without having to reconcile SAP and non-SAP data themselves, since Joule Agents and Joule Assistants draw on a harmonized SAP Business Data Cloud foundation. Teams receive role-based guidance for navigating complex workflows across Autonomous Domains, while everyday tasks such as retrieving information, connecting enterprise data, and completing multi-step processes happen independently, freeing staff from manual execution. In SAP Engagement Cloud, this means personalization and segmentation scale on their own, and the 4Q25 CX release lets customer service issues resolve autonomously, backed by SAP’s enterprise data layer and SAP Knowledge Graph, instead of requiring escalation. 

 Because Joule Studio is low code, organizations with reasonable levels of in-house development capabilities can build custom agents themselves, without waiting on IT or writing code, while still connecting to Joule, the SAP Customer Experience portfolio, and third-party systems grounded in SAP Knowledge Graph and SAP Business Data Cloud. For sales and marketing teams, this means faster deal cycles and higher conversion: a sales-assistant agent, for example, automatically surfaces buying patterns and product recommendations from purchase history, sparing reps the manual analysis. 

 Marketers running campaigns across email, digital ads, wallet, conversational, and web can manage them all from a single platform instead of stitching together point solutions. Because the engagement events service connects external data sources into real-time segmentation, campaigns stay relevant as customer behavior shifts. AI-assisted tools such as natural-language product search, AI-generated consumption summaries, and an AI-assisted report builder cut down the manual work of building segments and reporting, enabling marketers to focus on strategy while AI handles recommendations, translation, prediction, and reporting at scale. 

 AI that drives business results 

 Organizations around the world are using SAP’s AI-powered customer engagement capabilities to create more connected experiences and drive business results. For example: 

 Adler Mannheim uses an AI-powered data foundation to boost fan subscriptions by 50% and improve pre-game fan engagement by 80%. 

 Molton Brown combines AI-enhanced commerce and personalization to create seamless customer experiences that strengthen loyalty while maintaining 100% uptime during peak periods. 

 Douglas connects AI-driven shopping experiences, such as virtual beauty tools, and personalized product recommendations to deliver engaging and elevated customer experiences. 

 Advancing toward the Autonomous Enterprise 

 Being named a Leader in the IDC MarketScape: Worldwide Agentic Marketing for B2C Enterprises 2026 Vendor Assessment is an important milestone for SAP and the evolution of agentic marketing as a category. As organizations move from experimenting with AI to deploying agents that can reason, recommend, and act, we believe this recognition validates SAP’s approach of combining AI, trusted business data, and connected business processes to help customers navigate this next phase of transformation. 

 The vision of the Autonomous Enterprise is one in which AI-powered agents help organizations connect customer, operational, and business data to make and execute decisions with greater speed, relevance, and scale. In this future, AI doesn’t replace human expertise; it amplifies it. Intelligent assistants and agents can help teams act faster and more effectively, with governance and guardrails that keep people responsible for the strategy, creativity, and judgment that build lasting customer relationships. 

 Ultimately, the success of agentic AI will depend not only on what it can do, but on how much customers and businesses trust it to act on their behalf. 

 Learn more

items.text:
Hello QM experts, 
 I'm facing an issue in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition with the migration object QM - Quality Level. 
 Scenario 
 We use a Dynamic Modification Rule ( RD1) at Inspection Lot Level for inspection type 01 (Goods Receipt). 
 Inspection stages: 
 10 = Document check (Skip) 
 20 = Sampling inspection 
 30 = 100% inspection 
 The inspection plan is configured with: 
 Dynamic Modification Level = Inspection Lot Level 
 Dynamic Modification Rule = RD1 
 Usage = 5 (Goods Receipt) 
 Dynamic modification criteria = Material + Supplier (+ Manufacturer according to our configuration) 

 Migration 
 We migrated quality levels using the standard migration object and populated values similar to: 
 Material 
 Plant 
 Task List Type = Q 
 Task List Group = CONSO 
 Group Counter = 1 
 Supplier 
 Next Inspection Stage = 10 The migration completes successfully and, in Manage Quality Levels, the quality level is displayed correctly with: Next Inspection Stage = 10. 
 Issue 
 When performing the first Goods Receipt after migration: 
 SAP creates the inspection lot directly at stage 20 
 The migrated stage 10 is not used 
 The quality level appears to be ignored during inspection lot creation 

 Additional observations 
 If I manually set the quality level back to stage 10 afterwards, it remains at stage 10 and the skip logic works as expected. 
 Therefore the issue seems to occur only during the first inspection lot creation after migration. 
 I tried populating Inspection Type = 01 in the migration file because this value appears in SAP after lot creation, but the migration fails with error: QD665 - Inspection type not allowed for dynamization at inspection lot level 
 I also reviewed the customizing for inspection lot origins, inspection usages and dynamic modification criteria, but the behavior remains unchanged. 
 Question 
 Has anyone experienced this behavior? 
 Is there any known limitation of the QM - Quality Level migration object whereby only the inspection stage is migrated, but not the complete dynamic modification status/history required for SAP to use the migrated stage during the first inspection lot creation? 
 Or is there another field that must be migrated to ensure the first inspection lot starts at the migrated skip stage? 
 Any feedback would be greatly appreciated.

items.title: Using SAP Integration Suite AI Adapter to turn integration failures into actionable insights
items.author: EvertonMazzer
items.text:
Using SAP Integration Suite AI Adapter to turn integration failures into actionable insights 
 Introduction 
 Integration monitoring is an essential part of every integration landscape. 
 When customers have hundreds or even thousands of integrations running every day, monitoring becomes critical to identifying failed messages, understanding what happened, and taking corrective actions. 
 But there is an important question that goes beyond simply detecting a failure: 
 When an integration fails, how quickly can we understand what happened and what we should do next? 
 In many integration scenarios, the monitoring platform tells us that something went wrong. The next step still requires a person to open the Message Processing Log (MPL), analyze the failed step, inspect the backend response, and determine the probable root cause. 
 This is where I see an interesting opportunity for AI. 
 Instead of using AI to replace integration monitoring, we can use it to add an intelligence layer on top of the monitoring process. 
 In this blog, I will show a Proof of Concept using SAP Integration Suite, Cloud Integration, SAP Generative AI Hub, and the AI Adapter, where an integration failure automatically triggers an AI-based analysis that can be delivered to the team responsible for monitoring and support. 
 The Challenge: An Integration Error Is Often Just the Beginning 
 Imagine that an integration fails and the monitoring team receives: 

 HTTP 400 - Bad Request Technically, this is useful information. However, from an operational perspective, the investigation has just started. 
 The support analyst may need to: 
 Open the Message Processing Log. 
 Identify the failed step. 
 Inspect the backend response. 
 Understand which business process was being executed. 
 Identify the probable root cause. 
 Determine the business impact. 
 Decide whether the message can be safely reprocessed. 
 When this happens occasionally, this process is manageable. 
 When it happens hundreds of times across a large integration landscape, the amount of manual analysis can become significant. 
 This led me to explore a simple question: 
 What if AI could perform the first level of incident analysis when an integration fails? 
 The Concept 
 The idea is not to replace the Message Processing Log or the existing integration monitoring capabilities. 
 Instead, the architecture adds an AI-assisted analysis layer. 
 The traditional approach looks like this: 

 Integration Failure
 ↓
Monitoring
 ↓
Message Processing Log
 ↓
Manual Investigation
 ↓
Root Cause
 ↓
Action The proposed approach is: 

 Integration Failure
 ↓
Exception Subprocess
 ↓
Collect Error Context
 ↓
AI Adapter
 ↓
AI Incident Analysis
 ↓
Operational Notification
 ↓
Human Investigation / Action The AI provides the initial interpretation, while the existing monitoring capabilities remain available for detailed technical investigation. 
 Use Case 
 The use case is based on a Sales Order integration between an external application and SAP S/4HANA. 
 The external application sends a Sales Order request to SAP S/4HANA through SAP Integration Suite, Cloud Integration. 
 Under normal conditions, the integration processes the request and the Sales Order is created successfully. 
 However, if an error occurs during the integration, the scenario follows a different path. Instead of simply reporting the technical failure, the integration captures the available error context and sends it to the AI Adapter for analysis. 
 One important architectural principle here is that the AI processing only happens when an error occurs. 
 The normal business flow does not need to invoke the AI model. 
 This is an important point when thinking about AI in integration scenarios: 
 AI does not necessarily need to be part of every transaction. It can be activated when intelligence is actually needed. 
 Technology Components 
 The solution combines several capabilities of the SAP ecosystem: 

 The key point is that these components are combined into an incident-analysis flow, rather than using AI as part of every normal transaction. 
 Setting Up SAP Generative AI Hub 
 To implement this scenario, the AI capabilities are provided through SAP Generative AI Hub. 
 The Generative AI Hub provides a governed environment for accessing generative AI models and incorporating them into enterprise scenarios. 
 For this example, the AI model is used to analyze integration incidents and generate a structured troubleshooting response. 

 The exact model configuration can vary depending on the available models and the customer's SAP environment. 
 For this scenario, the important concept is not the specific model itself, but the ability to expose generative AI capabilities to the integration flow in a controlled way. 
 Configuring the AI Adapter 
 Once the AI environment is available, the next step is to configure the AI Adapter in SAP Cloud Integration. 
 The AI Adapter is used to invoke the AI capabilities from within the integration flow. 

 In the Service Key, the endpoint is provided under serviceurls as AI_API_URL. This value is used as the API endpoint when configuring the connection to SAP AI Core. 
 OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials 
 To connect SAP AI Launchpad and SAP Integration Suite to SAP AI Core, the required authentication information is obtained from a Service Key of the SAP AI Core service instance. 
 In SAP BTP Cockpit, navigate to the subaccount where SAP AI Core is provisioned and open the corresponding SAP AI Core service instance. 
 From the service instance, create a new Service Key and download or copy its credentials. 
 In this scenario, the AI Adapter is placed inside the Exception Subprocess. 
 This is intentional. 
 The AI service is not invoked for every successful Sales Order. 
 It is invoked when an integration failure occurs and additional analysis is required. 
 This creates an architecture where AI becomes an on-demand intelligence layer for integration incidents. 
 Defining the AI Prompt 
 The next step is defining what the AI should do with the integration error. 
 Rather than asking a generic question such as: 
 "What is wrong with this integration?" 
 the prompt defines a structured troubleshooting task. 
 For example: 

 You are an SAP Integration troubleshooting assistant.

Analyze the following integration incident.

SAP S/4HANA Error:
${property.error_message}

MPL ID:
${property.mpl_id}

Provide the analysis using the following structure:

1. Incident Summary
2. Probable Root Cause
3. Business Impact
4. Evidence
5. Investigation Points
6. Recommended Actions
7. Can the message be safely reprocessed?
8. Priority Level The structure of the prompt is important. 
 The goal is not simply to generate a natural-language answer. 
 The goal is to produce an output that can be used by an integration operations or support team. 
 Step 1 — Capture the Error Context 
 The first step in the Exception Subprocess is to capture the relevant error information generated by the integration. 
 For example, the HTTP layer may provide: 

 Bad Request : 400 : HTTP/1.1 
 However, the backend response can contain much more meaningful information: 

 Material TG1100 is not defined for sales org. 1410,
distr. chan. 10, OrProperty 'SoldToParty' has invalid value '14100009000' 

 The integration can extract the relevant error information and make it available to the AI analysis. 
 This distinction is important. 
 A generic HTTP status tells us: 
 Something failed. 
 The backend error can help explain: 
 Why it failed. 
 This is one of the key requirements for an AI-assisted monitoring scenario: 
 The AI needs meaningful context, not just an HTTP status code. 
 Step 2 — AI Analysis with the AI Adapter 
 Once the relevant error context has been prepared, the Exception Subprocess invokes the AI Adapter. 
 The AI receives the error information together with the instructions defined in the prompt. 
 The goal is to transform a technical exception into a structured incident analysis. 
 For example: 

 Technical Error
 ↓
AI Adapter
 ↓
Generative AI Model
 ↓
Structured Incident Analysis This is where the solution starts moving from monitoring toward intelligent operations. 
 Step 3 — Processing the AI Response 
 The AI Adapter returns the generated incident analysis. 
 The response can then be passed to the notification step, where it is included in the operational notification sent to the support or integration team. 

 The result is no longer just: 

 HTTP 400 Instead, the support team receives a structured analysis. 
 For example: 

 1. Incident Summary:
Sales Order creation failed in SAP S/4HANA.

2. Probable Root Cause:
Material TG1100 is not maintained for sales organization
1410 and distribution channel 10.

3. Business Impact:
The Sales Order could not be created.

4. Evidence:
Material = TG1100
Sales Organization = 1410
Distribution Channel = 10

5. Investigation Points:
Verify the material master and sales area data.

6. Recommended Actions:
Extend the material to the required sales area or
use a valid material.

7. Can the message be safely reprocessed?
No. The master data issue should be corrected first.

8. Priority Level:
High. The important difference is that the system has moved from: 
 Error Detection 
 to: 
 Contextual Analysis 
 Step 4 — Turning AI Analysis into an Operational Notification 
 Once the AI has analyzed the integration error, the result can be delivered to the team responsible for monitoring and support. 
 For this Proof of Concept, the AI-generated analysis is included in an automated notification. 

 The important point is that the notification is not intended to replace the monitoring platform. 
 It provides an AI-generated first analysis before the analyst starts the deeper investigation. 
 In our example, the notification is sent by email. However, the same AI-generated analysis could also be delivered through other channels, such as Microsoft Teams, SAP Alert Notification service, or an IT service management platform. 
 Where Could This Go Next? 
 This approach opens several possibilities for extending AI-assisted integration monitoring and intelligent operations. 
 Automatic Error Classification 
 Errors could be classified into categories such as: 
 Authentication 
 Authorization 
 Connectivity 
 Mapping 
 Transformation 
 Master Data 
 Business Validation 
 Backend Errors 
 Final Result 

 Final Result 

 After the integration failure is detected and analyzed, the AI-generated incident analysis can be delivered to the team responsible for monitoring and support. 
 In this example, the result is delivered by email. However, the same approach could be used to automatically create an incident or service ticket, send a notification through Microsoft Teams, or integrate with an IT service management platform. 
 The important point is that the support team receives more than a technical error message. The AI provides a structured first analysis that can help the team understand the incident and decide what to investigate next. 

 Example 1 — Invalid Material in SAP S/4HANA 

 Example 2 — Invalid Business Partner in SAP S/4HANA 

 Conclusion 
 This could help operations teams prioritize and route incidents. 
 When an integration fails, knowing that it failed is only the first step. 
 The real challenge is understanding what happened, why it happened, and what should be investigated next. 
 In this scenario, SAP Integration Suite, the AI Adapter, and SAP Generative AI Hub were combined to add an AI-assisted incident analysis layer to an existing integration monitoring process. 
 The goal is not to replace monitoring, logs, or the expertise of integration teams. Instead, AI can help transform technical error information into a structured starting point for investigation and action.

items.title: ISiK Certification for SAP Patient Management Extended Through May 2027
items.author: BettinaLieske
items.text:
ISiK Certification for SAP Patient Management Extended Through May 2027 
 (A german version of this blog post can be found below) 
 Great news from SAP Healthcare! 
 I'm pleased to share that gematik has extended the ISiK Level 3 certification for SAP Patient Management (IS-H) until May 31, 2027 . This ensures continued regulatory compliance for our customers while the German healthcare sector prepares for the next stage of interoperability. 
 A Brief Recap 
 As many of you know, SAP was the first hospital information system (HIS) vendor in Germany to receive gematik's confirmation for ISiK-compliant FHIR interfaces back in December 2021 — starting with ISiK Level 1 and the Base Module. In July 2025 , we reached another milestone when SAP Patient Management achieved ISiK Level 3 certification, covering both the Base Module and the Appointment Scheduling Module . 
 These certifications underscore our ongoing commitment to healthcare interoperability based on HL7 FHIR — an effort we have been driving since SAP Patient Management first introduced its FHIR interface framework in 2020. 
 Why an Extension? 
 ISiK standards are published in levels, each building on the previous one with additional modules and capabilities. The transition from Level 3 to Level 5 was originally expected to follow the established timeline. However, due to changes in § 371 (3) SGB V , the required ordinance under § 385 (1) SGB V — which defines the mandatory implementation deadline for ISiK Level 5 — was not issued in time. 
 Adding to the complexity, the emerging European Health Data Space (EHDS) regulation requires national interoperability standards like ISiK to be aligned with the new European Electronic Health Record Exchange Format (EEHRxF). With the EU implementing acts only expected by March 2027, industry stakeholders such as DKG have emphasized the need for coherent alignment between national ISiK requirements and European interoperability standards to avoid conflicting implementation obligations. 
 As a result, gematik has extended all valid ISiK Level 3 certifications to bridge the gap until ISiK Level 5 formally takes effect. This is a regulatory measure that affects all certified HIS vendors equally — it is not a reflection of any product-side delay. 
 What This Means for Our Customers 
 For hospitals running SAP Patient Management, nothing changes operationally . Your ISiK-compliant FHIR interfaces remain fully certified and legally valid through May 2027. Once the ISiK Level 5 timeline is finalized, we will plan for the next certification cycle. 
 We remain committed to driving interoperability in the German hospital landscape and will keep you updated as the regulatory framework evolves. 
 Want to learn more about ISiK and FHIR interoperability for SAP Patient Management? Check out my earlier posts: 
 SAP Patient Management achieves another milestone in Healthcare digitalization (ISiK Level 3) 
 SAP receives ISiK confirmation as first HIS manufacturer (ISiK Level 1) 
 ISiK-Zertifizierung für SAP Patient Management bis Mai 2027 verlängert 
 Gute Neuigkeiten von SAP Healthcare! 
 Ich freue mich, mitteilen zu können, dass die gematik die ISiK-Stufe-3-Zertifizierung für SAP Patient Management (IS-H) bis zum 31. Mai 2027 verlängert hat. Damit ist die regulatorische Konformität für unsere Kunden weiterhin sichergestellt, während sich das deutsche Gesundheitswesen auf die nächste Stufe der Interoperabilität vorbereitet. 
 Ein kurzer Rückblick 
 Wie viele von Ihnen wissen, war SAP der erste Hersteller eines Krankenhausinformationssystems (KIS) in Deutschland, der im Dezember 2021 die gematik-Bestätigung für ISiK-konforme FHIR-Schnittstellen erhalten hat — beginnend mit der ISiK Stufe 1 und dem Basismodul. Im Juli 2025 erreichten wir einen weiteren Meilenstein, als SAP Patient Management die ISiK-Stufe-3-Zertifizierung erhielt, die sowohl das Basismodul als auch das Modul Terminplanung umfasst. 
 Diese Zertifizierungen unterstreichen unser kontinuierliches Engagement für Interoperabilität im Gesundheitswesen auf Basis von HL7 FHIR — eine Initiative, die wir seit der Einführung des FHIR-Interface-Frameworks für SAP Patient Management im Jahr 2020 vorantreiben. 
 Warum eine Verlängerung? 
 Die ISiK-Standards werden in Stufen veröffentlicht, wobei jede Stufe auf der vorherigen aufbaut und zusätzliche Module und Funktionen umfasst. Der Übergang von Stufe 3 zu Stufe 5 sollte ursprünglich dem etablierten Zeitplan folgen. Aufgrund von Änderungen in § 371 Abs. 3 SGB V wurde jedoch die erforderliche Rechtsverordnung nach § 385 Abs. 1 SGB V — die die verbindliche Umsetzungsfrist für ISiK-Stufe 5 festlegt — nicht rechtzeitig erlassen. 
 Hinzu kommt, dass Verordnung zum Europäischen Gesundheitsdatenraum (EHDS) eine Abstimmung nationaler Standards wie ISiK mit dem neuen European Electronic Health Record Exchange Format (EEHRxF) erfordert. Da die EU-Durchführungsrechtsakte (Implementing Acts), die die genauen technischen Anforderungen definieren, werden erst bis März 2027 erwartet werden, haben Branchenverbände wie die DKG eine kohärente Abstimmung zwischen nationalen ISiK-Vorgaben und europäischen Interoperabilitätsanforderungen gefordert, um parallele oder widersprüchliche Umsetzungspflichten zu vermeiden. 
 Infolgedessen hat die gematik alle gültigen ISiK-Stufe-3-Zertifizierungen verlängert, um die entstandene zeitliche Lücke bis zum verbindlichen Inkrafttreten von ISiK Stufe 5 zu schließen. Es handelt sich dabei um eine regulatorische Maßnahme, die alle zertifizierten KIS-Hersteller gleichermaßen betrifft — und nicht auf eine produktseitige Verzögerung zurückzuführen ist. 
 Was bedeutet das für unsere Kunden? 
 Für Krankenhäuser, die SAP Patient Management einsetzen, ändert sich operativ nichts . Ihre ISiK-konformen FHIR-Schnittstellen bleiben bis Mai 2027 vollständig zertifiziert und rechtskonform. Sobald der Zeitplan für ISiK Stufe 5 feststeht, werden wir den nächsten Zertifizierungszyklus einplanen. 
 Wir setzen uns weiterhin für die Interoperabilität in der deutschen Krankenhauslandschaft ein und halten Sie über die Entwicklung des regulatorischen Rahmens auf dem Laufenden. 
 Möchten Sie mehr über ISiK und FHIR-Interoperabilität für SAP Patient Management erfahren? Lesen Sie meine früheren Beiträge: 
 SAP Patient Management erreicht einen weiteren Meilenstein in der Digitalisierung des Gesundheitswesens (ISiK Stufe 3) 
 SAP erhält als erster Hersteller die ISiK-Bestätigung (ISiK Stufe 1)
